chunks: Al-Mudaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Mudaffar al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud told us, from his father, saying: Jibril ibn Ahmad al-Faryabi told us, saying: Hasan ibn Khazrad told me, from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Furat, from Ya'qub ibn Suwayd ibn Mazeed al-Harithi, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, why was the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him) named the Commander of the Believers? He said: Because he grants them preeminence through knowledge. Have you not heard the Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'And We will provide for our family'?

key_terms.وَنُمِيرُ أَهْلَنَا: And We will provide for our family

ai.seo_question: Why is Imam Ali called the Commander of the Believers?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this etymological explanation linking 'Amir al-Mu'minin' to the root 'amara' (to lead or grant preeminence), specifically through the lens of divine knowledge. The Imam cites Surah Yusuf (12:65) to demonstrate that just as Jacob 'provided for' his family, Ali leads the believers to spiritual excellence through his superior knowledge. This interpretation highlights the Shia view that leadership (Imamah) is fundamentally rooted in esoteric and exoteric knowledge rather than mere political authority.
